content.text: {"headline":"Recommend no action (P0): the forecast shows both queues recovering to 99.3% service level with no changes needed.","why":"The 10:30 spike was caused by the P1 UPI switch outage (INC-20261006-6998). 213 payments calls arrived against 111.9 forecast, service level fell to 4.7% and 59 calls were abandoned. Staffing is at plan (42 of 43), handle time is below forecast and there were no campaigns, so this is an incident problem, not a staffing one. Going forward, the model predicts 99.3% service level on both payments and general and a 0.1% abandon rate if nothing changes, well above the 80% target. All plans cost the same (INR 15,939), so P0 is the simplest choice that meets the target.","trade_offs":["P1 (delay general breaks at 14:00) costs the same but predicts slightly lower results: 98.9% overall, 98.8% on general, 0.2% abandons. It disrupts agents for no gain.","P2 (delay breaks on both queues) breaks policy BRK-04, because 7 agents would have more than one break delayed today. It also predicts the lowest results: 98.1% overall, 97.4% on general.","P3 (break delay plus IVR callback on general) has the same predicted outcome as P1 (98.9%) at the same cost. It adds complexity with no benefit shown."],"watch":"The forecast assumes the UPI outage tail fades. Recent upi_payment_failed calls were 2.56x normal (183 vs 71.4 expected). If the incident stays open or payments arrivals climb again, re-run the plan. Keep P1 ready as a policy-compliant fallback around the 14:00 peak."}
